package_info.why_malicious: This report is a general overview of software supply chain security risks and does not analyze or identify any specific malicious package. It discusses the rise of supply chain attacks, the importance of securing open source dependencies, and the features of the Checkmarx One platform for mitigating these risks. No individual package or code is described as malicious.

behavioral_signatures: Unintentional exposure of secret credentials in public repositories
Use of vulnerable or malicious open source packages
Suspicious or unauthorized network communications from build or deployment pipelines
Automated scanning for secrets and repository health metrics
file_indicators: Presence of sensitive credentials (API keys, tokens, passwords) in source code or configuration files
Use of unmaintained or suspicious open source dependencies
CI/CD pipeline files with unexpected network or file access patterns
network_indicators: Outbound connections to unknown or suspicious domains from build or deployment environments
Unexpected API calls to external services during build or install processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor source code repositories for exposed secrets and sensitive credentials. Continuously scan open source dependencies for known vulnerabilities and signs of malicious behavior. Analyze CI/CD pipeline configurations for unauthorized network or file access. Use automated tools to assess repository health and prioritize remediation of high-risk components. Integrate security scanning into developer workflows and deployment pipelines to catch issues early.
